chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan, from Ibn Mukkan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the expiation of an oath: one feeds ten poor people, for each poor person a mudd of wheat or a mudd of fine flour and a handful, or their clothing, for each person two garments, or freeing a slave, and he has the choice among the three; whichever he does. If he cannot afford any of the three, then fasting for three days.

key_terms.مُدٌّ: A traditional unit of volume for dry goods

ai.seo_question: What are the options for expiating an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar details the specific measurements for kaffarat al-yamin, specifying ten muds of wheat or flour per person, which reflects the Shia emphasis on precise legal quantification (taqdir) in fiqh. It establishes a hierarchical structure of expiation, prioritizing material aid to the poor before resorting to fasting, thereby linking ritual obligation with social welfare. The narration underscores the flexibility granted to the individual to choose the most feasible option among the three primary means of expiation.
